summary.headline: Kajaria Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% to INR1,328 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.6%, driven mainly by fuel-cost-led price hikes.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to INR1,328 crore, mainly from selling price increases after gas costs rose following the Middle East conflict, while volume grew 6% despite a weak April. EBITDA margin expanded to 19.6% from 16.72% a year earlier, and PAT rose to INR169 crore from INR109 crore. Management guided to double-digit volume growth over the next nine months, an 18-19% full-year EBITDA margin, and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA, and announced two new capacity expansions (Srikalahasti and Gailpur). Morbi gas-price dislocation has narrowed the price gap between Kajaria and Morbi peers from about 40% to under 20%.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,162 crore, up 18% YoY; price increases were the main driver and the company is outsourcing part of volume from Morbi to meet demand this year.

segments.name: Bathware (Kerovit)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR122 crore, up 33% YoY; price hikes of about 15-16% and the rest volume. Management expects a tough margin year as restructuring continues, with FY27 value growth of 35-40%.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Revenue INR45 crore vs INR25 crore a year earlier; management says the segment is on track to grow much faster as branded share rises over informal players.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit volume growth expected over the next nine months (no volume guidance was given in the previous two quarters).
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 18-19% for the full year; EBITDA of INR1,000 crore+ targeted (management clarified EBITDA excludes other income).
Expects FY27 revenue growth of around 20%, with value growth of roughly 20% and double-digit volume growth; FY27 tile volume estimated at about 130 MSM vs about 118 MSM in FY26.
FY27 capex of roughly INR400 crore, including maintenance capex; Srikalahasti and Gailpur lines to spill over into next year.
Bathware to remain tough in FY27 with no margin guidance; management expects better value and profit in FY28.
Promoters have said they will not take salary this financial year; timing of future remuneration is undecided.
capex_capacity: Srikalahasti (South) brownfield expansion of 10 MSM at INR210 crore, approved at the last board meeting; about INR80-90 crore of this is a new shed.

Gailpur (Bhiwadi, Rajasthan) expansion of 11 MSM at INR165 crore, to be completed by April 2027; about INR40-50 crore is shed extension. Management expects INR370 crore to yield about 22 MSM in total across both sites, with turnover of INR400-450 crore per plant.
New lines use a 340-metre kiln versus 200 metres previously; machinery is a mix of SACMI and Chinese equipment.
Manufacturing capacity will not rise in FY27, so the company will outsource more from Morbi this year; dependence is expected to fall when the new plants start in Q1 FY28.
Approximately INR12 crore renewable energy acquisition was also mentioned.
demand_pricing: April was soft due to a full Morbi shutdown (March 5 to mid-April), pre-April dealer stocking in March, and labour shortages linked to elections and LPG supply. Management says May, June and July improved, with July growing double digits.

Gas costs in Morbi (GSPC-supplied) rose from about INR48 to INR86-88 per SCM, versus a 10-12% rise in North. Management says Morbi prices rose 40-45%, while Kajaria's North and South plants raised prices 10-13%.
Kajaria's price gap to Morbi narrowed from about 40% to under 20%; management says this shift is driving demand in North and East.

Management says the company is moving into institutional/project sales alongside retail, with two large builders won, and has about 1,800 dealers (450 exclusive), adding about 100 more this year (50 exclusive).
Geographic split: North 35%, South 30%, East 20%, West 15%. Channel: metro 15%, Tier 1 15%, Tier 2 30%, Tier 3 15%.
Exports are under 1% of turnover. Morbi exports fell to about INR1,000 crore per month from a higher pre-war run rate, due to higher freight costs.

Outsourcing: management said about 29-30% outsourcing currently; the FY27 mix is expected to rise before falling when new capacity comes on stream. Gas cost (blended average about INR71 per SCM in Q1; Morbi about INR85; spot about INR85).

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 11% realisation growth came from each segment, and where do price hikes go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Morbi cost increase was 40-45% versus 10-13% for North/South plants. Blended hikes were 13-14%, and non-Morbi plants took about 10%; prices are holding for now, but gas is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Where will double-digit volume growth come from in the next nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited May-June recovery, July continuing the trend, stronger distribution, project wins with two large builders, and new dealer showrooms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and how much is maintenance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex is about INR400 crore, including maintenance capex, with projects spilling over into next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why build in-house capacity now and what is the margin differential versus outsourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new lines are cheaper per MSM and more opex-efficient, and are highly ROC-accretive; outsourcing is used to fill near-term demand and is expected to fall next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA reach INR1,000 crore and when will promoters take remuneration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA and 18-19% margin for the year. The promoters have said they will not take salary this year, and the timing for later is undecided.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Bathware still weak and what margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a correction year after hiring a new CBO in April. It gave no margin guidance but expects 35-40% value growth in the segment for the year.

risks_watch: Gas supply and cost volatility: Morbi gas moved from about INR48 to INR86-88 per SCM after the war; management says the situation is very volatile and it cannot forecast post-Q1 gas prices, so the price-hike sustainability is unproven.

Delivery of double-digit volume growth over the next nine months: April was soft and July is only described as improving, so monitor monthly volume prints against the 130 MSM FY27 tile volume estimate versus about 118 MSM in FY26.
Outsourcing dependence: about 29-30% outsourcing now, expected to rise in FY27 because capacity is flat; Morbi-sourced margins and availability could move with Morbi gas costs.
Execution of Srikalahasti (10 MSM, INR210 crore) and Gailpur (11 MSM, INR165 crore) plants, with Gailpur due by April 2027 and new lines starting in Q1 FY28; FY27 capex of about INR400 crore.
Bathware remains a drag in FY27 with no margin guidance; restructuring and a new CBO hired in April; value growth target of 35-40%.
Export run-rate fell to about INR1,000 crore per month in Q1 FY27 versus about INR16,000 crore in FY26 due to freight costs, though exports are under 1% of Kajaria turnover.
key_quotes: If you recall, last 2 quarters, we have not given any volume guidance. But this year, with a lot of confidence, we are saying next 9 months, we'll have a double -digit growth.
So we are looking at an EBITDA margin about 18% to 19% for the entire year. First quarter, we already got 19.6%.
We have no choice really this year because of the production constraint, we will outsource from Morbi, that is the only option.
I would not like to give any margin guidance on sanitaryware and faucet side this year.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volume recovery, the 18-19% full-year EBITDA margin and the two capacity expansions, but was guarded and evasive on gas-cost outlook, forward pricing beyond the current level, and Morbi pricing, repeatedly saying the situation is too volatile to forecast. It declined to give segment-level or Morbi average realisation figures, spot gas detail, and institutional/retail split, and gave no margin guidance for Bathware.
